name: btor2-ind
notes: Bounded model checking that certifies what it proves: a greatest-fixpoint refinement first looks for an inductive, safe bit-invariant (state bits that never leave their initial constant) and writes it as a certificate; otherwise BMC deepens and after each proven depth the plain k-induction step is tried from an arbitrary state, the proven depths being the base for free; a closed step is written as a k-induction certificate. Failing both, the plain BMC verdict: a self-replayed witness, a bounded all(k), or an honest partial. Every certificate is {"schema": "induction", "payload": ...}, discharged by btor2@2's judge at the stop and never taken on faith; at admission all three universal corpus items discharged. Bit-vector fragment with the signed division family; arrays refused with a partial. Budgets derive from the wall argument, never the clock. Era-6 revision 1 = the Era-5 btor2-ind text re-cut with the v6 certificate envelope. Revision 2 blasts the signed division family (sdiv, srem, smod — the same construction as btor2-bmc: magnitudes through the unsigned divider, signs fixed after) and evaluates it in the self-replay interpreter, and turns every remaining unsupported op into a partial instead of a crash; thirteen svcomp25-mini programs and four hwmcc24-mini programs crashed the first revision on sdiv/srem. Byte-identical on the predecessor corpus. Revision 3 runs on the bounded checker's array engine: arrays (sort array, read, write, array ite, extensional eq/neq, symbolic array inputs and states) enter by the eager reduction, and k-induction's step is tried on such machines exactly as on bit-vector ones; bit-invariants range over bit-vector states only. Byte-identical on the predecessor corpus; two array machines join the corpus.
